## 2.0 Chapter Prerequisites

::: {.callout-note icon=false title="Function composition"}
**Function composition** refers to combining functions in a way that the output
from one function becomes the input for the next function. In other words, the
range ($y$-values) of one function become the domain ($x$-values) of the next
function. We denote this as $(f \circ g)(x) = f\big(g(x)\big)$, where the output of
$g(x)$ becomes the input of $f(x)$.
:::

## 2.1 Instantaneous Rates of Change: The Derivative

::: {.callout-warning icon=false title="Definition 2.1.1 — Derivative at a Point"}
Let $f$ be a continuous function on an open interval $I$ and let $c$ be in $I$.
The **derivative of $f$ at $c$**, denoted $f'(c)$, is
$$
\lim_{h\to 0} \frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h},
$$
provided the limit exists.
:::

::: {.callout-warning icon=false title="Definition 2.1.2 — Tangent Line"}
Let $f$ be continuous on an open interval $I$ and differentiable at $c$, for some
$c$ in $I$. The line with equation $\ell(x) = f'(c)(x - c) + f(c)$ is the
**tangent line** to the graph of $f$ at $c$; that is, it is the line through
$\big(c, f(c)\big)$ whose slope is the derivative of $f$ at $c$.
:::

::: {.callout-warning icon=false title="Definition 2.1.3 — Derivative Function"}
Let $f$ be a differentiable function on an open interval $I$. The function
$$
f'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}
$$
is the **derivative** of $f$.

**Notation:**

Let $y = f(x)$. The following notations all represent the derivative:
$$
f'(x) = y' = \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{df}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}(f) = \frac{d}{dx}(y).
$$
:::

## 2.2 Interpretations of the Derivative

::: {.callout-important icon=false title="Key Idea 2.2.1 — The Derivative and Motion"}
(a) Let $s(t)$ be the position function of an object. Then $s'(t)$ is the
velocity function of the object.

(b) Let $v(t)$ be the velocity function of an object. Then $v'(t)$ is the
acceleration function of the object.
:::

## 2.3 Basic Differentiation Rules

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.3.1 — Derivatives of Common Functions"}
| | |
|---|---|
| 1. **Constant Rule:** $\dfrac{d}{dx}(c) = 0$, where $c$ is a constant. | 2. **Power Rule:** $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^n) = nx^{n-1}$, where $n$ is any real number. |
| 3. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x$ | 4. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x$ |
| 5. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^x) = e^x$ | 6. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ln x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$ |
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.3.2 — Properties of the Derivative"}
Let $f$ and $g$ be differentiable on an open interval $I$ and let $c$ be a real
number. Then:

(a) **Sum/Difference Rule:**
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\big(f(x) \pm g(x)\big) = \frac{d}{dx}\big(f(x)\big) \pm \frac{d}{dx}\big(g(x)\big) = f'(x) \pm g'(x)
$$

(b) **Constant Multiple Rule:**
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\big(c \cdot f(x)\big) = c \cdot \frac{d}{dx}\big(f(x)\big) = c \cdot f'(x).
$$
:::

::: {.callout-warning icon=false title="Definition 2.3.1 — Higher Order Derivatives"}
Let $y = f(x)$ be a differentiable function on $I$.

(a) The *second derivative* of $f$ is:
$$
f''(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\big(f'(x)\big) = \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = y''.
$$

(b) The *third derivative* of $f$ is:
$$
f'''(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\big(f''(x)\big) = \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right) = \frac{d^3y}{dx^3} = y'''.
$$

(c) The *$n^{\text{th}}$ derivative* of $f$ is:
$$
f^{(n)}(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\big(f^{(n-1)}(x)\big) = \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{d^{n-1}y}{dx^{n-1}}\right) = \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = y^{(n)}.
$$
:::

## 2.4 The Product and Quotient Rules

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.4.1 — Product Rule"}
Let $f$ and $g$ be differentiable functions on an open interval $I$. Then
$f \cdot g$ is a differentiable function on $I$, and
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\big(f(x)g(x)\big) = f(x)g'(x) + f'(x)g(x).
$$
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.4.2 — Quotient Rule"}
Let $f$ and $g$ be differentiable functions defined on an open interval $I$, where
$g(x) \neq 0$ on $I$. Then $f/g$ is differentiable on $I$, and
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right) = \frac{g(x)f'(x) - f(x)g'(x)}{\big[g(x)\big]^2}.
$$
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.4.3 — Derivatives of Trigonometric Functions"}
| | |
|---|---|
| 1. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x$ | 2. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x$ |
| 3. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \sec^2 x$ | 4. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot x) = -\csc^2 x$ |
| 5. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec x) = \sec x \tan x$ | 6. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\csc x) = -\csc x \cot x$ |
:::

## 2.5 The Chain Rule

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.5.1 — The Chain Rule"}
Let $y = f(u)$ be a differentiable function of $u$ and let $u = g(x)$ be a
differentiable function of $x$. Then $y = f\big(g(x)\big)$ is a differentiable
function of $x$, and
$$
y' = f'\big(g(x)\big) \cdot g'(x).
$$
:::

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.5.2 — Generalized Power Rule"}
Let $g(x)$ be a differentiable function. Then
$$
\frac{d}{dx}\Big(g(x)^n\Big) = n \cdot \big(g(x)\big)^{n-1} \cdot g'(x).
$$
:::

## 2.6 Implicit Differentiation

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Theorem 2.6.1 — Glossary of Derivatives of Elementary Functions"}
Let $u$ and $v$ be differentiable functions, and let $c$ and $n$ be real numbers,
$n \neq 0$.

| | |
|---|---|
| 1. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(cu) = cu'$ | 2. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(u \pm v) = u' \pm v'$ |
| 3. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(u \cdot v) = uv' + u'v$ | 4. $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right) = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$ |
| 5. $\dfrac{d}{dx}\big(u(v)\big) = u'(v)\,v'$ | 6. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^n) = nx^{n-1}$ |
| 7. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(c) = 0$ | 8. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x) = 1$ |
| 9. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ln x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$ | 10. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^x) = e^x$ |
| 11. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x$ | 12. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x$ |
| 13. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \sec^2 x$ | 14. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot x) = -\csc^2 x$ |
| 15. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec x) = \sec x \tan x$ | 16. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\csc x) = -\csc x \cot x$ |
:::
